description: R14 robustness closure: right-sized resource/soak targets (plan section 'Resource and soak tests -- right-sized'). This file is a CONFIG for the soak runner. The cutoverBlocking runner landed with FCOMP-E (crates/dohc-workspace-engine/src/bin/dohc-soak-runner.rs, harness feature): it drives these scenarios against a real composed daemon and writes self-describing evidence JSON (recorded tolerances, explicit RSS/drain dispositions, workload and drain sample series) to tools/rust-engine-program/soak-evidence/.

smoke.description: PR-gate-sized subset, runs in every `cargo test --workspace` invocation via crates/dohc-engine-runtime/tests/soak_r14.rs. Proves the open/close-returns-actor-count-to-baseline MECHANISM at small scale; does not attempt OS-level thread/handle/RSS measurement.
assertions: WorkspaceSupervisor::actor_count() returns to exactly 0 after every single close
close_all() returns actor_count() to exactly 0 regardless of how many distinct workspace identities were opened

cutoverBlocking.description: The plan's REQUIRED pre-cutover soak (Gate 6 evidence). Driven by dohc-soak-runner; the one-line verdict is pasted into EXECUTION_LOG.md as evidence per the program's convention, with the full evidence JSON committed beside it.
scenarios: plain workspace open/close cycling (the smoke tier's scenario, at full scale)

watcher storms (continuous filesystem change bursts, exercising WATCH_HARD_DEADLINE flush -- see crates/dohc-engine-files/tests/watch.rs::continuous_event_stream_still_flushes_at_the_hard_deadline for the unit-scale version of this scenario)
cancellation storms (many concurrent request cancellations against the protocol Supervisor and the daemon's request-admission path)
editor open/update/close cycles (Y.Doc apply + settle under sustained load)
assertionsMeasuredByRunner: threads/OS handles return to baseline after all workspaces close, within the runner's RECORDED tolerances (handleSlack 48, threadSlack 8 -- Windows OS handle counts jitter across a run from runtime/OS-owned handles, so exact-zero is not a stable cross-run assertion; the evidence JSON records absolute baseline/final counts so any drift is auditable, and the accepted slacks are emitted under 'tolerances')

RSS steady-state trend plus unaided idle-drain classification: maxRssSlopeBytesPerSec remains 20480 and applies to the simple linear fit over the final half of workload samples, not the warm-up-dominated whole run. That tail is evaluated only when it independently has >= 24 samples spanning >= 900s (otherwise trendEvaluated:false and rssDisposition NOT-EVALUATED cannot be cited as leak evidence). Evidence always records rssSlopeBytesPerSecWholeRun, rssSlopeBytesPerSecTail, the per-quarter slope series, the tail sample count/span, and warmupDominatedWholeRunFit; a tail PASS with an over-bound whole-run fit is therefore explicit rather than silently presented as a bare fit PASS. After work stops, the same daemon stays alive for a 120s drain sampled at the existing 5s cadence; the runner does not call malloc_zone_pressure_relief, madvise-style purge, or any allocator release API. With >= 5 drain samples, RECLAIMED requires the drain-end RSS to return >= 75% of baseline-to-drain-start growth (leaving <= 25% retained near the pre-run plateau); otherwise the drainDisposition is RETAINED, and too few samples is NOT-EVALUATED. An over-bound tail fit becomes the distinct rssDisposition RETAINED-RECLAIMED only when drainDisposition is RECLAIMED; a run that neither stays within the tail slope bound nor reclaims remains FAIL. Evidence also records drain start/end/min RSS, run growth, drop bytes and percent, counters, thresholds, allocator policy, and the full workload and drain series.

scenario correctness: every cycle's requests succeed (a failed or hung request panics the run -- per-request 60s bound, 30s handshake bound, in-flight requests failed on daemon death), and every crash/restart cycle recovers
clean daemon shutdown: exits within 30s of stdin close AND with a successful exit status (cleanShutdown in the evidence)
assertionsNotMeasuredByThisRunner: queues return to steady state after bursts -- NOT directly measured; queue depths are bounded by construction (bounded mpsc admission + command channels) and R14's daemon-liveness tests cover admission under pressure; a PASS verdict makes no claim here (the evidence lists this under unmeasuredAssertions)

workspace close returns owned resources to baseline plus a documented constant -- covered at unit scale by crates/dohc-engine-runtime/tests/soak_r14.rs (actor_count returns to exactly 0); the runner only observes process-level handles/threads, so the per-resource claim is NOT re-measured here

no unbounded WAL/update-log/replication-log/index growth under compaction/retention scenarios -- NOT yet measured by any runner; tracked for the postCutoverContinuous tier and dogfood-period monitoring
trackedMetrics: SQLite connection count and WAL size
queue depths (protocol Supervisor admission, files actor command queue)
shutdown duration (the daemon drain-before-close path R14 added -- see crates/dohc-workspace-engine/src/bin/dohc-workspace-engine.rs)

postCutoverContinuous.description: Explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this shard and for Gate 6 -- the plan places these post-cutover, running continuously during the dogfood window rather than as a cutover-blocking gate ('the founder is the canary and dogfood time is free soak time').
postCutoverContinuous.note: Same trackedMetrics as cutoverBlocking, with statistical trend bounds over the longer window. No runner exists for this tier; the cutoverBlocking runner and its dogfood-period monitoring results should shape it.
